To preserve the score in its original units
questions.answer: To map it to a probability between zero and one
questions.explanation: The sigmoid converts the unrestricted fitted score into the bounded probability scale.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 4: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A fitted logistic regression coefficient is positive. Holding the other predictors fixed, what happens to the event odds as that predictor increases?
choices: They become unrelated to the coefficient
questions.explanation: A positive coefficient raises the fitted log odds, and odds move in the same direction.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 4: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: Under the naive Bayes model, when are predictor values assumed to be independent of one another?
questions.explanation: It factors the predictors' joint distribution separately within each class.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 4: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A model assigns each flower exactly one of four species names. Which task is this?
questions.explanation: The label belongs to more than two mutually exclusive classes.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 4: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A tree sends cases left or right according to whether a measurement exceeds a cutoff. What is this part of the tree?
questions.explanation: An internal node applies a rule to split cases between child branches.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A standard regression tree uses squared error. Which summary of the training responses is stored as a terminal prediction?
choices: The arithmetic mean of the responses in that leaf
The median response in the root
The largest response in that leaf
The average response of neighbouring leaves
questions.answer: The arithmetic mean of the responses in that leaf
questions.explanation: For a constant prediction, the arithmetic mean minimizes the sum of squared differences in the leaf.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A tree fitter compares nested smaller trees using a score that penalizes extra terminal leaves. What approach is this?
questions.explanation: The method trades training error against the number of leaves.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A planner fits trees on bootstrap samples and averages their predictions. Every tree can consider all features for each split. Which method is described?
questions.explanation: Bagging averages models fitted to bootstrap samples without a random-feature restriction.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: An ensemble trains bootstrap trees and gives each split a freshly sampled subset of predictors. Which method uses both choices?
questions.explanation: A random forest decorrelates its bagged trees by restricting split candidates.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A model adds shallow trees one at a time to reduce the loss left by the current ensemble. Which method matches this?
questions.explanation: Boosting fits successive additions to improve the ensemble's current predictions.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 8: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A margin classifier relies on a subset of training cases on or inside the margin to define its separating rule. What are those cases called?
questions.explanation: Support vectors are the training examples with nonzero contributions to the margin classifier.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 9: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A classifier evaluates inner products in a richer feature space without explicitly constructing those features. What technique makes this possible?
questions.explanation: A kernel supplies the inner products directly.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 9: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: An analyst explores patterns in hundreds of sensor records without a known outcome column. Which learning setting is this?
questions.explanation: The inputs are available without labelled responses.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A museum groups visits with similar movement patterns without predefined visitor labels. Which task is it solving?
questions.explanation: Clustering finds groups of similar observations without known classes.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: During a k-means update the memberships stay fixed. What location is assigned to each cluster representative?
choices: The centre obtained by averaging its member coordinates
The member closest to the origin
The midpoint of the most distant two clusters
The least dense location in the cluster
The same point chosen for all clusters
questions.answer: The centre obtained by averaging its member coordinates
questions.explanation: A k-means centroid is the coordinate-wise average of its assigned points.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: During k-means assignment, which cluster receives a point when the centroids are held fixed?
questions.explanation: Each point goes to the centroid with minimum squared distance.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: What quantities does standard k-means sum in its objective?
questions.explanation: The objective adds the squared distance from each point to its assigned centroid.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A team repeats k-means with several starting centroid sets. What is the purpose?
questions.explanation: Different starts can converge to different solutions. Repetition can find one with lower within-cluster error.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: An agglomerative method starts with one cluster per item. What operation builds successively larger clusters?
questions.explanation: It merges an eligible pair selected by the linkage criterion.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A dendrogram cut is moved above several extra merge heights. How does the cluster count change?
questions.explanation: The new cut includes more merges, leaving fewer separate groups.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: Which linkage can connect two long groups if only one cross-group pair is very close?
questions.explanation: Single linkage uses the closest pair across the two groups, so one close bridge can be enough.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: A team wants two groups to merge only when every cross-cluster pair is within a set distance. Which distance should drive the merge?
questions.explanation: Complete linkage measures the most distant pair between the two groups.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: Which linkage takes all the distances between members of different groups and gives each pair the same weight?
questions.explanation: Average linkage takes the mean of the cross-group distances.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: DBSCAN finds a point with too few neighbours that is also unreachable from any core point. How is it labelled?
questions.explanation: It belongs to neither a dense core nor its reachable boundary.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: Under DBSCAN, a point's radius neighbourhood contains at least min_samples points counting itself. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: Meeting the minimum neighbourhood count makes it a core point.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: A point has a strongly negative silhouette value. What does that suggest?
choices: Its own cluster is very compact around it
It is equally close to both clusters
Its label is known to be correct
questions.explanation: Its mean distance to another cluster is smaller than to its own.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: A clustering's label names are permuted but every pair of points has the same group relationship. What happens to its adjusted Rand score against a fixed reference?
questions.explanation: The score compares pairwise group membership, so names do not matter.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Clustering: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html

questions.clue: What distinguishes the first principal component direction among unit-length directions?
questions.explanation: Its projection of the centered data captures the most variance.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: An analyst wants the weights on the original variables that define a component axis. Which quantities should they inspect?
questions.explanation: Loadings specify the direction's coefficients on the measured features.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A student projects each country's measurements onto the first component axis. What are the resulting coordinates called?
questions.explanation: A score locates one observation on a principal component axis.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: What does a large fraction of variance explained by the first principal component indicate?
choices: One direction captures much of the variation
Every later direction has equal variance
There are no large residuals for any point
questions.answer: One direction captures much of the variation
questions.explanation: The fraction compares variation along that component with total variation across components.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A PCA should give comparable prior weight to variables measured in dollars and kilograms. What preprocessing addresses scale differences?
questions.explanation: Standardization puts each feature on a comparable variance scale.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 12: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A filter flags a message as spam, and manual review confirms it is spam. Which confusion-matrix cell gains one?
questions.explanation: The prediction and the actual class are both positive.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A screen flags a valid library card as expired. The positive class is expired. How is this prediction counted?
questions.explanation: It predicts positive for a genuinely negative case.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A detector misses a dent on a panel, with dent the positive class. Which type of error occurred?
questions.explanation: A positive case received a negative prediction.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A sensor correctly labels a good tile as free of defects, with defect the positive class. Which cell does it enter?
questions.explanation: The actual label and prediction are both negative.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: Of all items flagged by a detector, which metric asks how many of those flags are genuine?
questions.explanation: This metric uses predicted positives as its denominator.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A factory wants to know how often equipment faults are detected among the faults that actually occur. Which metric should it report?
questions.explanation: Recall starts with actual positive cases and asks what fraction the detector finds.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: Which metric measures correct rejections among cases that really are negative?
questions.explanation: A genuinely negative case counts toward specificity when the classifier calls it negative.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: Among pages that are truly clean, which quantity measures the share incorrectly flagged as errors?
questions.explanation: A false alarm is a predicted positive among the actual negatives.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: Which expression gives F1 from precision P and recall R?
questions.explanation: F1 is their harmonic mean, which requires their sum in the denominator.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: An ROC curve puts true-positive rate on its vertical axis. What is on the horizontal axis?
questions.explanation: The curve traces true-positive rate against false-positive rate as the threshold varies.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A classifier lowers the score required to predict positive. What can happen to its true-positive and false-positive counts on the same cases?
questions.explanation: The larger set of positive predictions may contain additional real positives and negatives.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: A detector always predicts the majority label. Why can accuracy look good on a strongly imbalanced test set?
choices: Accuracy gives the common class most of the weight
Accuracy treats both classes as equally frequent
Accuracy excludes any missed rare cases from its denominator
Accuracy averages the two class recalls equally
questions.answer: Accuracy gives the common class most of the weight
questions.explanation: The majority class contributes most of the cases to an ordinary accuracy score.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification

questions.clue: How can a reliability diagram check the calibration of a probability model?
choices: Compare predicted probabilities with observed frequencies
Compare feature means with feature variances
Compare training time with prediction time
Compare sample sizes with class counts
Compare feature ranks with coefficient ranks
questions.answer: Compare predicted probabilities with observed frequencies
questions.explanation: The diagram checks whether observations assigned similar probabilities occur at similar frequencies.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Probability calibration: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html

questions.clue: Cases scored near 0.80 are positive only about half the time in a large holdout. What does this indicate for that score range?
questions.explanation: Observed frequency is well below predicted probability, indicating overprediction in that range.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Probability calibration: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html

questions.clue: Which practice distinguishes ordinary k-fold validation from a single fixed validation split?
choices: Rotate which subset is held out
Use one permanent test split throughout
Tune only on the test set
questions.answer: Rotate which subset is held out
questions.explanation: Each subset serves as the holdout while other blocks supply training data.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 5: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A dataset contains four scans per person. A model must generalize to new people. How should validation be split?
choices: Train and test on all scans
questions.explanation: Keeping each person's scans together avoids testing on people represented in training.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Cross-validation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html

questions.clue: A team evaluates a model for next month's demand. Which split best reflects deployment over time?
questions.explanation: Forecasting evaluates future observations after fitting on earlier ones.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Cross-validation: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html

questions.clue: Within a cross-validation run, what data should determine the mean used to center a feature?
questions.explanation: Estimating the mean only from the training fold leaves the validation fold independent of preprocessing.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Common pitfalls, Data leakage: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html#data-leakage

questions.clue: A model predicts at order time whether a refund will occur. Which feature risks leaking the outcome?
questions.explanation: The actual refund amount is generated after the prediction moment and reveals the outcome.
questions.reference: scikit-learn user guide, Common pitfalls, Data leakage: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html#data-leakage

questions.clue: A team tunes all settings using validation data and keeps a separate untouched set. What should the untouched set be used for?
questions.explanation: After choices are fixed, the test set estimates performance on fresh data.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 5: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: Between a network's measurements and its final score, a set of learned units transforms the inputs. What is this layer called?
questions.explanation: It is internal to the network, between input and output.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: Which feature of max(0, x) separates this activation from the identity function?
choices: The flat segment for negative inputs
A flat segment for positive inputs
questions.answer: The flat segment for negative inputs
questions.explanation: It transmits positive inputs and maps negative inputs to the same output.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/
questions.math_clue: Which feature of $\max(0,x)$ separates this activation from the identity function?

questions.clue: If every layer applies only an affine transformation, what is the combined network before the loss?
questions.explanation: Compositions of affine maps are still affine. Nonlinear activations change that.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A program applies the chain rule from the loss through the network to obtain weight derivatives. Which procedure is this?
questions.explanation: Backpropagation carries derivative information backward through each layer.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: In wₜ₊₁ = wₜ − η∇L(wₜ), which term sets the scale of each step?
questions.explanation: The learning rate scales the component subtracted from the current weight.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/
questions.math_clue: In $w_{t+1}=w_t-\eta\nabla L(w_t)$, which term sets the scale of each step?

questions.clue: An optimizer uses 32 training examples to estimate the gradient for its next update. What are those 32 examples called?
questions.explanation: A mini-batch is the subset used for one update.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A network has processed one full pass through its training set. What has it completed?
questions.explanation: An epoch covers the entire training set once.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A trainer randomly zeros selected hidden activations on each training update to limit co-adaptation. What method is this?
questions.explanation: Dropout makes the network train with a changing subset of active units.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: Training loss keeps falling but validation loss starts rising. The trainer restores the weights with the best validation loss. What technique is this?
questions.explanation: Stopping at the best validation point can avoid fitting training noise.
questions.reference: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, chapter 10: https://www.statlearning.com/

questions.clue: A text pipeline divides a sentence into units that will be mapped to integer IDs. What is this step called?
questions.explanation: Tokenization defines the units the model consumes.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Words and Tokens: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/2.pdf

questions.clue: A tokenizer encodes an unfamiliar word as several reusable fragments rather than introducing a word-specific ID. Which scheme is described?
questions.explanation: Reusable fragments allow previously unseen words to be represented by known pieces.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Words and Tokens: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/2.pdf

questions.clue: What history does a standard bigram model use to predict the next token?
questions.explanation: It conditions on the immediately preceding token.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, N-gram Language Models: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/3.pdf

questions.clue: An autoregressive text decoder has just sampled one token. What happens before it predicts the next one?
choices: Use the generated token as context
questions.answer: Use the generated token as context
questions.explanation: The sampled token joins the prefix that conditions the next prediction.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Transformers and Pretraining: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/7.pdf

questions.clue: A decoder always emits whichever token has the largest probability at the current step. Which strategy is it using?
questions.explanation: Greedy decoding makes a locally best token choice each step.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Transformers and Pretraining: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/7.pdf

questions.clue: Keeping unequal logits fixed, a decoder increases a positive temperature before applying softmax. How do the token probabilities generally change?
choices: A uniform distribution at all temperatures
questions.explanation: Dividing the logits by a larger temperature reduces score gaps and makes the probabilities more even.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, Transformers and Pretraining: https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/7.pdf

questions.clue: During decoder-only training, which positions must a token be prevented from attending to if it predicts the next token without a future leak?
questions.explanation: The causal mask blocks access to positions beyond the current one.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.clue: An attention head has computed probabilities over input positions. Which vectors does it combine with those probabilities?
questions.explanation: Attention weights multiply value vectors to form the output.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.clue: In scaled dot-product attention, which factor divides the query-key dot product when keys have dimension dₖ?
questions.explanation: The square root scaling limits growth in logit magnitude with key width.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
questions.math_clue: In scaled dot-product attention, which factor divides the query–key dot product when keys have dimension $d_k$?

questions.clue: A translation decoder uses queries from its own states and keys and values from the encoded input sentence. What attention pattern is this?
questions.explanation: The queries come from a different sequence than the keys and values.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.clue: A Transformer computes several independently projected attention outputs in parallel and then combines them. Which component is this?
questions.explanation: Multiple projected heads can focus on different patterns before their outputs are combined.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762

questions.clue: Attention layers receive token embeddings and an added signal for where each token appeared in the sequence. What is this signal?
questions.explanation: Positional encoding communicates token order to an attention model.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.5: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
